Experiment_Name: Reconcile UCI Benchmark Documentation & API Metadata
Problem_Being_Addressed: Test window boundary discrepancy (4,503 vs 4,421 kWh) in backend config and status reports
Proposed_Change: Update backend/config.py and frontend telemetry displays to document both full-test (4,503 kWh) and boundary-trimmed (4,421 kWh) windows explicitly.
Expected_Benefit: Eliminates conflicting numbers across API and documentation with zero code risk
Success_Criteria: All reported numbers match single source of truth ledger
Evaluation_Method: Automated regression test against metric ledger

Problem_Being_Addressed: Fold-2 CV MAE blowout (37,169 kWh) caused by 2011 customer meter onboarding
Evidence_from_Existing_Work: Fold-2 MAE is 37,169 kWh due to 2011 mean load (122k) vs 2012 mean load (212k)
Proposed_Change: Restrict TimeSeriesSplit to the stationary operational regime (2012-2013 training data, ~17,500 hours) where all 370 meters are active.
Expected_Benefit: CV Mean MAE stabilizes to ~4,200 - 4,800 kWh, aligning cross-validation with true generalization performance.
Success_Criteria: CV Mean MAE < 5,000 kWh with Std < 1,000 kWh

Experiment_Name: Promote LightGBM Focal Loss to Production Backend
Problem_Being_Addressed: Baseline XGBoost achieves Test PR-AUC=0.3114 and F1=0.3592, limited by standard binary cross-entropy on imbalanced data.
Evidence_from_Existing_Work: LightGBM Focal Loss (gamma=2.0, alpha=0.85) achieved Test PR-AUC=0.4178 (+34.2%), ROC-AUC=0.8429, F1=0.4479 in results/optimization_v2/sgcc_focal_loss_comparison.csv.
Proposed_Change: Integrate models/optimization_v2/lgbm_focal_loss_best.joblib into backend/inference/sgcc_predictor.py behind an opt-in model configuration flag.
Expected_Benefit: +34.2% lift in PR-AUC and +24.7% lift in Test F1 without changing the 18-feature inference API contract.

Problem_Being_Addressed: Fixed decision threshold t=0.50 treats false positives and false negatives with arbitrary equal weight, ignoring real-world utility economics.
Evidence_from_Existing_Work: Threshold operating curve (results/optimization_v2/sgcc_threshold_operating_curve.csv) shows inspection hit rates vary from 18% to 65% depending on threshold.
Proposed_Change: Implement utility cost matrix: Cost = C_insp * FP + C_stolen * FN - Recovered_kWh * TP. Compute optimal threshold maximizing net utility revenue.
Expected_Benefit: Translates F1 score into quantified utility dollar recovery; allows operators to tune threshold to field inspection capacity.
Success_Criteria: Demonstrate net cost reduction over fixed t=0.50 baseline
Evaluation_Method: Parametric cost simulation across inspection budget tiers

Experiment_Name: UCI Causal Lag & Difference Expansion (Delta Forecasting)
Problem_Being_Addressed: Direct load regression suffers slight lag-1 inertia; model predicts absolute levels rather than instantaneous hourly rate-of-change.
Evidence_from_Existing_Work: SHAP analysis shows load_t and lag_1 account for >80% feature weight; tree-based models struggle with sudden peak inflection points.
Proposed_Change: Formulate difference forecasting: predict delta_y_{t+1} = y_{t+1} - y_t using demand difference features (y_t - y_{t-1}, y_t - y_{t-24}, y_t - y_{t-168}). Reconstruct y_{t+1} = y_t + delta_hat.
Expected_Benefit: Forces model to learn genuine acceleration/deceleration dynamics; eliminates non-stationarity drift; expected MAE reduction of 5-10%.
Success_Criteria: Test MAE < 4,000 kWh on sealed test set

Problem_Being_Addressed: Handcrafted scalar summary features destroy temporal ordering and sequence shape; consumption overlap exceeds 95%.
Evidence_from_Existing_Work: Literature (Arif et al. 2021) suggests deep residual representations capture subtle sequential theft signatures that summary statistics miss.
Proposed_Change: Train a 1D Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) or ResNet-1D on raw 1,034-day daily sequences using contrastive or masked autoencoding pretraining, followed by supervised fine-tuning.
Expected_Benefit: Discovers non-linear temporal motifs (sudden step-drops, gradual bypass drift) without relying on aggregate missingness counts.
Success_Criteria: Test F1 > 0.48, PR-AUC > 0.45 without missingness features

Problem_Being_Addressed: Ground truth labels contain un-inspected thieves labeled as 0 (false negatives in ground truth), capping model precision at ~35-40%.
Evidence_from_Existing_Work: SGCC_DATASET_LIMITATION_AUDIT.md confirms benign class has >95% overlap with theft and learning curves plateau, pointing to label contamination.
Proposed_Change: Apply Elkan-Noto or Bagging PU Learning to reweight unlabeled (FLAG=0) instances, estimating the true unobserved prior p(s=1|y=0).
Expected_Benefit: Down-weights contaminated normal instances during gradient computation, boosting precision without sacrificing recall.
Success_Criteria: Test Precision increases to >0.45 at 50% recall

Problem_Being_Addressed: Tree regressors cannot extrapolate beyond training extremes; Linear/Ridge models extrapolate but lack non-linear interaction capacity.
Evidence_from_Existing_Work: Linear Regression achieved R2=0.9764 in 0.04s; XGBoost achieved R2=0.9923; residuals show complementary error distributions.
Proposed_Change: Build a two-stage hybrid model: Ridge predicts linear baseline trend, XGBoost predicts residual error (e_t = y_t - y_hat_ridge).
Expected_Benefit: Combines robust trend extrapolation with non-linear tree precision; improves robustness to unprecedented grid demand spikes.
Success_Criteria: Test MAE < 4,100 kWh, improved peak-load accuracy

Problem_Being_Addressed: High forecast residual spikes occur on Portuguese public holidays (Easter, Christmas, New Year) where industrial demand drops dramatically.
Evidence_from_Existing_Work: Residual error plot (graphs/uci/forecasting/02_forecast_error_over_time.png) exhibits sharp localized error spikes on national holidays.
Proposed_Change: Add binary Portuguese national holiday indicator and bridge-day flags using Python holidays package.
Expected_Benefit: Reduces holiday forecast error spikes by 40-60%; expected overall MAE reduction of 50-100 kWh.

Experiment_Name: Reproduce SMOTE-NearMiss Hybrid from Arif et al. (2021)
Problem_Being_Addressed: Investigate whether published SMOTE-NearMiss claims translate to genuine generalization on an untouched test set.
Evidence_from_Existing_Work: Arif et al. report high accuracy using SMOTE-NearMiss, but NearMiss removes boundary samples, creating artificial margins.
Proposed_Change: Implement SMOTE-NearMiss inside training folds; compare against class-weighting and Focal Loss on the sealed test set.
Expected_Benefit: Empirical proof of whether published SMOTE-NearMiss gains are an artifact of balanced test sets or hold in realistic deployment.
Confidence: POSSIBLE (Likely to cause high false positives)
Risk: Medium (NearMiss often destroys natural decision boundaries)
Success_Criteria: Demonstrate whether PR-AUC improves over Focal Loss
